summary: Iteration 13 full validation of the Treasure Standard™ Improvement Loop, Enterprise Readiness Review + Factory Acceptance Test endpoints, publish gate, product review, Enterprise Command Center panels, Founder Security Banner, and 7 navigation pages. All 9 backend pytest tests PASSED in 219s (including the LLM-heavy Treasure Standard loop end-to-end). Backend: /api/enterprise/readiness returns readiness_score=100, overall='ready', 8 checks all pass, recipes=45, packages=21. /api/enterprise/factory-acceptance-test returns enterprise_quality_score=99, 12 modules (Analytics=90 by design, everything else 100), lifecycle[] present, production_ready=false because Analytics<100. Treasure Standard loop: manufactured a Blog Article on a Verified KR — order completed in ~2 minutes, product published with verified=True and treasure_standard=True; production_order_id linkage confirmed; NO founder click required. Publish gate: PATCH /api/products/{pid}/status→Published on unverified product returns 400. Review endpoint: reject→Rejected persists; approve→Published+verified=True; nonexistent id→404. Founder auth: temporary-password flags set (using_temporary_password=true, setup_required=true) — Founder password NEVER changed. Frontend: Founder logged in successfully; Enterprise Command Center renders 6 division cards, readiness-panel (100% Ready to scale), founder-security-banner with working 'Set Permanent Password' toggle (opened → 3 form fields visible → closed without submitting), Factory Acceptance Test button clicked → fat-panel rendered with all 12 fat-module-0..11 cards showing scores + notes. /teach page has topic-input, package select, and enabled start-manufacturing-btn. All 7 required nav pages (teach, topic-registry, orchestrator, verification-team, product-protection, integration-hub, ai-services) load without pageerrors and expose their primary buttons.

issues: The Enterprise Command Center™ link appears in the top 'THE QRU EXPERIENCE' section AND another 'Command Center' link is in the 'MISSION CONTROL' section. Slightly confusing — both go to different pages (/command-center vs /) but the naming makes them look duplicate. Consider renaming or clearer grouping.

FAT enterprise_quality_score is 99 (Analytics hardcoded to 90 until payments wired) yet production_ready=false because the check requires ALL modules ≥100. Copy currently reads '99% · Ready to scale' from readiness (which is 100%), but the FAT badge shows amber. Not a bug — expected per spec — but the two adjacent 99/100 badges may confuse users. Consider surfacing 'Production ready when payment provider is connected' hint next to the amber badge.

action_items: OPTIONAL polish: add tooltip/hint next to FAT badge explaining that reaching 100% requires connecting a payment provider (Analytics module = 90 by design).
OPTIONAL: preserve the well-known React 'hydration <span> in <option>' console warning from the Emergent visual-editor instrumentation — still present on /teach; not the app's fault.
critical_code_review_comments: product_protection.treasure_finalize does up to (max_rounds+1)=3 verify calls + 2 improve calls per product = up to 5 LLM calls per product. For 1-product manufacture this is ~2-4min as designed. However bulk/package manufacture (Full Package = 45 recipes) could burn hundreds of LLM calls. Recommend a hard client-side confirm on Full Package/Meditation Package in ProductionLine.js and Orchestrator.js.

product_protection._improve_product truncates current content to 4000 chars — for long products (Sleep Story, Interactive Lesson) the improve pass may only see the first 4KB and lose downstream context. Consider chunked improvement or summary+diff strategy.

routers/enterprise.factory_acceptance_test 'production_ready' requires ALL modules ≥100 but Analytics Division is hardcoded to 90 until payments wired — meaning production_ready will always be false until commerce is integrated. Consider either: (a) exclude 'connected connectors' modules from the strict gate, or (b) surface 'production_ready_when_payment_connected: true' as a separate field.

routers/enterprise.readiness 'Automation' check marks 'warn' when hands_free_mode is OFF but the operator may intentionally turn it off during launches; this could scare readers into thinking the factory is broken. Consider labelling 'informational' vs 'warn' for operator-toggled states.

product_protection.treasure_finalize on 'escalated' path (LLM parse fail or exception) sets status=Needs Review but doesn't insert a founder_escalations row for that specific case — only the max-round-exhaustion path creates an escalation. If the LLM verifier itself crashes, the product sits in Needs Review without any founder-visible escalation. Consider inserting an escalation on the escalated path too.

Sidebar Navigation duplicates 'Command Center' (Dashboard route /) and 'Enterprise Command Center™' (/command-center) — both use LayoutDashboard icon and similar names. Suggest renaming one (e.g. 'Dashboard' vs 'Enterprise Command Center™') for disambiguation.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (Founder login + Enterprise Command Center full workflow (6 divisions, readiness-panel, run-fat-btn → 12 fat modules), founder-security-banner toggle, /teach form, and all 7 required nav pages verified)

seed_data_creation: Manufactured 1 Blog Article via /api/automation/manufacture/{kr_id} — completed, published, treasure_standard=true. Rejected an existing product via /api/automation/products/{pid}/review (decision:reject), then approved a Needs Review/Rejected product via review approve which re-published it. Verified escalations endpoint returns [] (no open quality escalations after loop, meaning improvement loop successfully hit standard without needing founder).

Treasure Standard loop LLM cost: ~5 LLM calls per product (verify → improve → verify → improve → verify). Full Package (45 recipes) would be ~225 calls — DO NOT run bulk in future testing.
rca of the issue: No bugs identified in iteration 13. The only 'quirk' is that FAT.production_ready is always false because Analytics module is hardcoded to 90 until payments are wired — this is by design per the mocked_apis list ('Revenue analytics not connected — Analytics module scores 90 by design until a payment provider is wired'). The Enterprise Quality Score of 99% correctly reflects this. Recommend main agent add a UI hint or separate 'production_ready_when_payments_connected' field to remove the amber signal, but this is non-blocking.
